# devin-orchestrator

> Background-worker fan-out policy for Devin Desktop: a skill/rule pair plus a deterministic planner CLI that decides how many subagents a task may spawn.

devin-orchestrator solves the problem of uncontrolled (or absent) parallelization in Devin sessions: the model needs to know when to fan a task out into background workers, and the hard limits must live in code, not in prose the model can argue away. It ships three layers: (1) a `.devin/skills/devin-orchestrator/` skill and an always-on `.devin/rules/background-workers.md` rule that instruct the model to fan out when a task has 2+ independent units or large scope, (2) a deterministic planner (`devin-orchestrator plan '<json-signals>'`) that takes structured task signals and returns how many workers are allowed (absolute cap: 3, `DEVIN_MAX_WORKERS` can only lower), which profile to use (`subagent_general` vs read-only `subagent_explore`), and enforced constraints — 0 workers for trivial/question tasks, nesting forbidden under `DEVIN_INSIDE_SUBAGENT=1`, `collect=true` on every fanned-out plan, and (3) a persistent SQLite task queue (`devin-orchestrator queue submit|claim|done|fail|sweep|collect|status` + `queue fanout` for worktree-locked units) that the coordinator submits to and workers claim from — atomic BEGIN IMMEDIATE claims, heartbeat-renewed leases, orphan recovery via sweep, bounded retries with idempotency keys, and secret-screened payloads. The plan is data only and the queue only records/locks: no paths become commands, no workers are spawned, no filesystem writes beyond the local store. Unofficial community tooling, not affiliated with Cognition AI.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/Icaro0310/devin-control/blob/main/packages/orchestrator/README.md): full documentation and workspace install steps

## Key commands

- `uv tool install devin-fanout  # CLI: devin-orchestrator; or: pipx install devin-fanout`: install the planner CLI (Python >= 3.10)
- `devin-orchestrator plan '{"kind":"implementation","independent_units":3,"needs_write":true,"estimated_scope":"large","summary":"API + UI + tests"}'`: compute a worker plan as JSON (`workers`, `mode`, `profiles`, `collect`, `limits`)
- `devin-orchestrator plan '<spec>' --files src/a.py,src/b.py`: one constrained work unit per declared file (collision-checked like `units_detail`)
- `devin-orchestrator queue submit '<json>'` / `queue claim --worker W` / `queue done <id> --worker W`: the local SQLite task queue — atomic leased claims, `queue sweep` for orphan recovery, `queue collect` before the aggregate report
- `devin-orchestrator queue fanout <repo> --branch NAME --files ...`: submit a unit targeting an isolated git worktree with a physical worktree+branch lock and file-collision refusal
- `cp -R devin-orchestrator/.devin/skills/devin-orchestrator .devin/skills/` + `cp devin-orchestrator/.devin/rules/background-workers.md .devin/rules/`: install the skill and always-on rule into a Devin workspace
- `pytest -q`: behavioral matrix test suite (trivial -> 0, units -> min(N,3), nested -> 0, ...)

## When to use / when not

- Use when: your Devin sessions run large multi-part tasks serially when they could fan out; you want worker caps enforced in code (max 3 concurrent, no nesting) rather than as prompt suggestions; you want read-only `subagent_explore` workers for investigation and write-capable ones only where needed; you already use Devin's background-subagent support and want a policy layer on top.
- Not when: you expect the CLI to spawn workers itself (it only computes a JSON plan — the skill/rule supplies instructions and Devin's runtime executes them); you are not on Devin (the policy only makes sense inside Devin's subagent model); your tasks are inherently serial or single-unit (the planner correctly returns 0 workers anyway); you need more than 3 concurrent workers (the cap is absolute by design).
